The spec is clear on the status workflow, required fields, and what is out of scope. One behavior is still open, and it changes validation, the edit screen, and tests.

**Question:** After a ticket is closed or cancelled, can an agent still change its details and add comments?

Why it matters: This decides whether edit and comment actions stay available on a finished ticket, and whether the system must reject those saves.

**Recommended:** Option B — The spec already allows edits and comments on any existing ticket, and the source requirements do not freeze a ticket when it is closed or cancelled. Keeping those actions available avoids new rejection rules that no current acceptance scenario requires.

| Option | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| A | Finished tickets are view-only. No field changes, no resolution-note changes, and no new comments. |
| B | Finished tickets stay editable. Title, description, priority, assignee, resolution notes, and new comments are still allowed. Status still cannot change. |
| C | Resolution notes and new comments are still allowed. Title, description, priority, and assignee are locked. |
| D | New comments are still allowed. Every other field is locked. |

You can reply with the option letter (e.g., "A"), accept the recommendation by saying "yes" or "recommended", or provide your own short answer.

Recorded in the spec: a closed or cancelled ticket can still have its title, description, priority, assignee, and resolution notes changed, and it can still receive comments. The status stays as it is.

**Question:** Does a search keyword match part of a word in the title or description, or only a whole word?

Why it matters: A search for "pay" either includes a ticket titled "payment" or leaves it out, and the search tests have to assert one of those results.

**Recommended:** Option A — The spec already says a ticket matches when the title or description contains the keyword, using a case-insensitive phrase match. "Contains" means the keyword appears as a contiguous substring, so a fragment such as "pay" matches "payment", and a multi-word keyword must appear in that order.

| Option | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| A | Contiguous substring. "pay" matches "payment". A phrase such as "payment failure" must appear in that order, ignoring case and surrounding spaces. |
| B | Whole words only. "pay" does not match "payment". A multi-word keyword must appear as those whole words in order. |
| C | Exact field match. The title or the description must equal the keyword, ignoring case and surrounding spaces. |

You can reply with the option letter (e.g., "A"), accept the recommendation by saying "yes" or "recommended", or provide your own short answer.

/speckit-plan Only write files inside the current feature folder.
Monorepo: backend/ (Maven, Java 21, Spring Boot 3.5: Web, Validation, Data JPA, Flyway, PostgreSQL driver, Testcontainers) and frontend/ (React + Vite + TypeScript, react-router, typed fetch client).
docker-compose.yml at the root using pgvector/pgvector:pg16 (reused in Phase 2).
Package by feature: ticket, comment, common.
State machine: TicketStatus enum with an allowed-transitions map; status changes only through PATCH /api/tickets/{id}/status; PATCH /api/tickets/{id} cannot change status.
Errors: RFC 7807 ProblemDetail per api-standards.mdc (400 with field errors, 404, 409 for invalid transitions).
GET /api/tickets?q=&status=&page=&size=.
Seed ~15 realistic tickets with comments and resolutions (payment failures, shipment tracking, login issues) via a Flyway migration.
Tests: state machine unit tests, a @SpringBootTest + Testcontainers parameterised test over all 25 status pairs, and @WebMvcTest for validation.
Keep user stories small so each one can be implemented and committed separately.
